_schema: canonical_findings v1 (assimilation-lifecycle-protocol 2026-07-15). Future experiments must state which findings constrain them. classification in the protocol's fixed set.

findings.claim: The flat-action SAC critic divergence (crit loss 0.66->72.7) was an IMPLEMENTATION confound, not fundamental: it came from the hardcoded initial entropy coefficient (alpha0=1.0) and learning rate (1e-3). With alpha0=0.1 + LR 3e-4 the critic stays bounded (0.18-4.61).
findings.confidence: measured (single-seed diagnostic, mechanism verified)
findings.scope: flat-action SAC on PlanarGrasp; the stable hyperparameters generalize to BC-anchored SAC refinement
findings.limitations: alpha0=0.1/LR3e-4 is task-tuned; NOT promoted to the global SACConfig default (would change classic-SAC behavior on other envs).
findings.framework_consequence: Coin-toss/flat SAC refinement drivers must set init_alpha=0.1, LR 3e-4 (recorded discipline). SACConfig now exposes init_alpha; entropy schedule via AlphaMode.

findings.claim: There is NO SAC integration bug in the actor mechanics: BC gradient is live and in the same action space as behaviour_clone (anchor MSE 5e-4 post-BC), sign correct, tanh log-prob sane, freeze-actor holds delivery (eval path consistent), overfit+reload exact.
findings.confidence: measured (7 fixed-batch tests)
findings.scope: SquashedGaussianActor + train_sac actor update
findings.limitations: mechanics-only; says nothing about closed-loop delivery
findings.framework_consequence: The integrity suite is a reusable diagnostic pattern (fixed-batch gradient/space/sign/freeze/overfit) for any actor-loss contradiction.

findings.claim: The 'BC penalty ~70 should dominate but the actor drifts' contradiction is explained by GRADIENT MAGNITUDE, not loss magnitude: |g_BC|=0.040 is 15% of the full actor gradient, dwarfed ~5x by entropy (|g_entropy|=0.205) and ~3x by -Q (0.116); cos(g_BC,g_entropy)=-0.20 (entropy OPPOSES the anchor).
findings.confidence: measured
findings.scope: flat-action SAC actor loss (entropy + -Q + demo anchor)
findings.limitations: measured on PlanarGrasp; the ranking (entropy>Q>anchor) is env/reward-scale dependent
findings.framework_consequence: Explains why TD3+BC (no entropy) holds while classic SAC drifts; motivates entropy-schedule component + rollout-anchor.

findings.claim: Entropy control (alpha fixed-low / annealed / ~0) does NOT rescue flat-action delivery: all ladder arms collapse the 0.417 BC floor online (S3 alpha~0 -> 0.000). Entropy explained the gradient magnitude but is not the delivery cause.
findings.confidence: measured, 5 arms x 3 seeds x 25k
findings.scope: flat per-step action abstraction on the floorless PlanarGrasp env
findings.limitations: does NOT close the flat path entirely — the rollout-state anchor (F-SAC-5) is a separate untested lever
findings.framework_consequence: Flat per-step SAC pipeline QUARANTINED (registry); entropy schedule is a speed lever, not a delivery fix. Guard: do not deploy a flat per-step SAC actor as a coin-toss default.
findings.open_questions: Does rollout-state DAgger anchoring rescue it? (flat_sac_rollout_state_dagger_anchor, running)

findings.claim: The demo-state anchor holds action_mean AT BC on demo states (dist_from_bc ~0.002 across all 15 cells) yet closed-loop delivery collapses to ~0 ⇒ the destructive change is on ROLLOUT states the demo-state anchor never covers (covariate shift), not action drift on demo states.
findings.confidence: measured (15 cells, consistent)
findings.scope: any BC-anchored refinement of a reactive policy on a floorless env
findings.limitations: mechanism inferred from the dist/delivery double-signal; the fix (rollout anchor) is being tested
findings.framework_consequence: Motivates sac.rollout_state_dagger_anchor (EXPERIMENTAL). A demo-state-only anchor is INSUFFICIENT against covariate shift — future BC-anchor refinement should consider rollout-state supervision.
findings.open_questions: Confirmed positive pending flat_sac_rollout_state_dagger_anchor full run.

findings.claim: Delivery must be graded at the env's success_steps DWELL and the demonstrator ceiling measured FIRST: a hardcoded dwell>=20 (vs success_steps=5) read the 0.9-delivery demonstrator as 0.000, nearly mis-attributing a harness bug as a covariate collapse.
findings.confidence: measured (demonstrator 0.000 -> 0.9 after fix)
findings.scope: all coin-toss / flat delivery evaluation
findings.limitations: specific to dwell-graded delivery tasks
findings.framework_consequence: Canonical delivery metric (eval_delivery / flat_metrics) reads success_steps, never a literal. Measure the demonstrator ceiling before ranking a policy (CLAUDE.md eval-integrity rule, now with a concrete on-record catch). NOW DECLARABLE: meta_evaluation.hymeko carries grade_dwell + ceiling_first + disjoint cohorts; enforcement (validate grade_dwell==env.success.steps) is the follow-up.

findings.claim: The deployed FANUC pick-place policy is a Markov-mode hybrid-DAgger clone of the v3 clean expert on the require_settle task: 0.875 stable-place / 4.69 cm. The v3 expert resolves the clean-vs-yield conflict by a BASIN CONSTRAINT (route v2's clean transit into v1's unflipped grasp basin), reaching 0.906 / 2.16 cm.
findings.confidence: measured (multi-seed DAgger + clearance test)
findings.scope: fanuc pick-place v3+settle, fixed target
findings.limitations: raw state_dict (no metadata); target-blind; precision imitation-bounded.
findings.framework_consequence: controller.pick_place_hybrid_dagger_base registered DEPLOYABLE; loaded via load_pick_policy.
code_changes: already integrated (this assimilation added the compat-validated loader route)

findings.claim: Offline actor-critic (TD3+BC) COLLAPSES on FANUC pick-place: crit/act blow up, rl_refined (0.0-0.4375) <= bc_step0. BC/DAgger is the working imitation path; from-scratch/warm-start PPO also collapses to ~0.
findings.confidence: measured (multiple runs, value-drift signature)
findings.scope: fanuc pick-place env/reward
findings.limitations: scoped to this env; not a universal TD3+BC impossibility.
findings.framework_consequence: pick_place_td3bc + pick_place_ppo + pick_place_rl_sidebyside labeled NEGATIVE_DIAGNOSTIC/SUPERSEDED in the registry (kept runnable for repro, must not become default).

findings.claim: Structured residual RL HOLDS the frozen base 0.875 exactly (anchor + settle reward + PPO + mode-gate) but CANNOT improve it: a bounded action-residual cannot move a feedback controller's setpoint. Precision floor stays ~4.6 cm; SAC entropy drifts it.
findings.confidence: measured (delta x reward x mode-set grid, 3 seeds)
findings.scope: residual RL as a PRECISION lever over the frozen base; from-scratch RL NOT closed
findings.limitations: closure scoped to bounded residual over a frozen setpoint.
findings.framework_consequence: ResidualPickEnv registered RESEARCH_ONLY (not deployed); the closure is recorded so a later branch does not re-adopt residual-as-precision-lever silently.
findings.open_questions: From-scratch asymmetric actor-critic (not setpoint-bound) for precision — untested.

findings.claim: Pick-place precision is IMITATION-BOUNDED (~4.7 cm): no clone reaches the expert's 2.16 cm across feedforward, centered-target, and every recurrent cell (GRU/LSTM/peephole/LN/CIFG) — the centering is execution-hard, drowned in the BC loss. LSTM WINS reliability (0.917). Cloning a MORE-precise (centered Markov) target BACKFIRES (0.667/5.31, more-precise=harder-to-clone).
findings.confidence: measured (confound-controlled on common-settled episodes)
findings.scope: precision by IMITATION; a stateful RL-from-scratch or an obs exposing the PI integral are NOT closed
findings.limitations: the 2.16cm is a stateful-PI mechanism not observable to a feedforward clone.
findings.framework_consequence: Guard: a more-precise scripted target is not automatically a better clone target — do not re-run centered-target cloning expecting a precision gain. LSTM is the reliability-canonical recurrent cell.
code_changes: control/pick_place_laws.py centered laws REVERTED to tool-at-target (this backfire recorded)
findings.open_questions: DAgger'd target-aware/LSTM past the 7.5cm tolerance — untested.

findings.claim: Clones are TARGET-BLIND (the target is not in the base observation; the hypergraph is arm-only) so they MEMORISE the fixed training target — a moved target misses by 17.5 cm. Adding target feedback (observe_target: object->target displacement in node_features) + varied-target training makes a clone place at an ARBITRARY target (moved-target 1.45 cm).
findings.confidence: measured (moved-target end-to-end)
findings.scope: fanuc pick-place arbitrary-target placement
findings.limitations: target-aware reliability borderline (0.71-0.79) at the 7.5cm tolerance.
findings.framework_consequence: env.observe_target_feedback registered CANONICAL (default off, byte-identical); load_pick_policy validates observe_target so a target-aware clone cannot be loaded into a target-blind env (or vice versa).
code_changes: gui build_scene builds env obs to match ckpt

findings.claim: Pick-place checkpoint provenance was UNSAFE: every FF/HSiKAN/TD3 checkpoint is a raw state_dict with NO metadata; the June checkpoints use an obs-72 schema incompatible with the current obs-90; and 4 uncentralized loaders (only the GUI's validated). A wrong-schema checkpoint could mis-load or fall back silently.
findings.confidence: measured (discovery over ~200 checkpoints; obs-72 vs obs-90 confirmed by tensor shapes)
findings.scope: all pick-place checkpoint loading
findings.limitations: provenance sidecar for the metadata-blind FF base still recommended (deferred).
findings.framework_consequence: loader.load_pick_policy (+ load_pick_actor + PickPolicyIncompatible) is now THE loader used by build_scene / render_trained / residual_rl._load_base; it FAILS LOUD on obs/action/observe_target mismatch (never a silent mis-load). Also: reports/models/campaign/* are galambos, NOT pick-place -> excluded from the manifest. NOW DECLARABLE: meta_provenance.hymeko carries the load recipe (kind/algo/arch_signature) + reward_hash/seed/eval_cohort; loader-reads-provenance (vs the GUI filename guess) is the follow-up.
code_changes: gui/pick_place_scene.py, viz/render_pick_place.py, pick_place_residual_rl.py routed through it
findings.open_questions: Re-defaulting PickPlaceEnv bare constructor (still builds the anthropomorphic/v1/no-settle config) — deferred to a fail-loud guard, separate authorization.

findings.claim: The legacy success predicate (delivered = held-above-target) inflated 'place' rates until require_settle (genuine set-down: object at rest, released, within radius) was introduced. All pre-settle place rates are on the LEGACY metric and must not be compared across the boundary. The two '0.875's (v1-dirty-legacy vs v3-clean-settle) are different cohorts.
findings.confidence: measured
findings.scope: all pick-place evaluation
findings.limitations: require_settle default off (byte-identical legacy); canonical spec sets it on.
findings.framework_consequence: Canonical env spec is expert_version=3 + require_settle=True; PlacementPrecisionMetric/LiftPlaceMetric carry the divergence guard (a blow-up must not count as a lift/settle). Do not merge pre/post-settle place rates.
code_changes: already integrated (require_settle in the canonical spec)

findings.claim: A structure-aware elimination ordering cuts direct-solve fill-in on structured constraint graphs: min-degree gives 4.3x less fill than natural order on a cloth grid and 14.5x less on a pile, while every ordering blows up on a truly dense pile. Fill-in is the exact proxy for direct sparse-solve (Cholesky/LDL) cost.
findings.confidence: measured (fill/width/flops under 4 orderings x 3 system classes x 7 sizes, deterministic seeds)
findings.scope: constraint graphs of physics scenes (bodies=nodes, joints '+'/contacts '-' = signed edges)
findings.limitations: fill is a proxy for the factor cost, not wall-clock (that is F-PHYS-2); Sigma-deg^2 flops is the classic dense-Cholesky proxy.
findings.framework_consequence: The ordering + elimination-cost primitives are canonical (physics.structural_cost_predictors); solve cost is predictable from the graph BEFORE solving.

findings.claim: The direct-vs-iterative wall-clock crossover IS a treewidth threshold: structured/articulated systems (tw <= sqrt(N): chain, cloth<=N576, the real arm) solve fastest EXACTLY by sparse-direct (residual ~1e-16), dense piles solve fastest ITERATIVELY by CG (e.g. pile N=1024: CG 1.50 ms vs direct 7.82 ms, 5.2x). The fill proxy becomes seconds and accuracy.
findings.confidence: measured (SuperLU MMD_AT_PLUS_A direct + CG, median of 5 reps, seeded)
findings.scope: SPD/bilateral constraint solve (A = L + lambda*I over the constraint graph)
findings.limitations: A = L + lambda*I is the constraint-graph sparsity proxy, not the exact Delassus/KKT operator; CG is the bilateral-block analog of PGS; wall-clock constants are Python/scipy-prototype (F-PHYS-6).
findings.framework_consequence: Motivates the certificate-routed solver (F-PHYS-3): the crossover is predictable from the width, so it can be automated.
findings.open_questions: Grounding on the exact MuJoCo efc_* / KKT operator (box-pile) remains.

findings.claim: A single cheap structural number — the SBSH width certificate (a treewidth upper bound the scene already carries) — routes the constraint solve to the best of {exact-direct, iterative-CG} across the whole structure spectrum, with measured worst-case regret 1.13 vs an oracle that always picks the faster method (~1.0 almost everywhere). It recovers exactness where cheap (residual ~1e-16, where always-CG settles for ~1e-8) AND dodges the direct-factor blow-up where not.
findings.confidence: measured (regret over chain/cloth/pile x 7 sizes + the real MuJoCo arm; residuals exact)
findings.scope: any bilateral/SPD constraint solve exposing a (positions, signed-edges) graph
findings.limitations: W*=40 is one calibrated threshold (production: a fill-vs-iters cost model); the certificate's own cost is assumed amortised via incremental width maintenance (L5, conditional on edit locality; L6: adversarial global edits force Omega(sqrt N)); constants are Python-prototype (F-PHYS-6).
findings.framework_consequence: EXTRACTED to the canonical framework: AdaptiveWidthSolver + certificate_width in hymeko_rl/sbsh_scene/solver.py, exposed from the package __init__, imported by the physics_adaptive driver (no longer defined there). Future SBSH physics work imports it (anti-bloat).
findings.open_questions: A production cost model (fill vs iters*N) instead of a width cutoff; incremental certificate maintenance under adversarial edits.

findings.claim: The REAL frictional-contact solve obeys the same law: an LCP with Coulomb friction solved by Projected Gauss-Seidel over the Delassus-structured coupling has PGS iterations and #colours (parallel phases) CONSTANT in N on structured contact graphs (chain 19->19, cloth 40->43, arm 20; colours 3/6/3 constant) and GROWING on dense piles (iters 28->207, colours 4->32, accuracy 1e-5->9e-4, wall-clock to 2.2 s). So the width certificate predicts the real contact solver's cost and parallelism, not just the linear proxy.
findings.confidence: measured (PGS to 1e-6, median of 3 reps, seeded; the real MuJoCo arm graph included)
findings.scope: frictional rigid-body contact LCP over the contact line graph
findings.limitations: coupling is Delassus-STRUCTURED (line-graph Laplacian + I), not the exact J M^-1 J^T from an engine (topology faithful incl. the arm; entries a well-conditioned model); friction is a Coulomb box on one tangential; PGS accuracy is the honest ~1e-5, degrading with density; Python inner loop sets the wall-clock constants (F-PHYS-6, iteration/colour counts are implementation-free).
findings.framework_consequence: EXTRACTED to the canonical framework: ContactLcpSolver + contact_coupling/greedy_colors/pgs in solver.py, imported by the physics_lcp driver (no longer defined there). physics.contact_lcp_solver is CANONICAL.
findings.open_questions: Extract MuJoCo's true efc_* on a box-pile scene (the exact-Delassus grounding step).

findings.claim: The octree/spatial nested-dissection ordering is a WEAKER heuristic than min-degree on degenerate graphs: on a 1-D chain (true treewidth 1) it over-separates to induced width 2, while min-degree recovers the exact optimum (width 1, fill 0). It is a valid ordering (a permutation, and it does reduce grid fill vs natural), but it is NOT the clean structure-aware order.
findings.source_experiment: sbsh-physics-probe (2026-07-11, honest test failure kept as a finding)
findings.confidence: measured (elimination width under all three orderings on chain/cloth)
findings.scope: elimination orderings for the width certificate
findings.limitations: a production nested-dissection (METIS) would not over-separate; this is the octree-separator heuristic specifically.
findings.framework_consequence: GUARD: certificate_width uses MIN-DEGREE, not octree-ND. A regression test pins certificate_width(chain)==1 so a refactor cannot silently swap in the weaker heuristic. order_nested_dissection is retained as a measured heuristic, flagged in physics.structural_cost_predictors.known_limitations.

findings.claim: The SBSH physics numbers are a Python/scipy PROTOTYPE. The STRUCTURAL conclusions — scaling exponents, PGS iteration counts, #colours, the regret 1.13 — are implementation-free and citable. The wall-clock CONSTANTS are not: a Rust/C inner loop would cut them ~1-2 orders (exponents unchanged). No real-time (games/physics) claim may rest on the prototype constants.
findings.confidence: measured caveat (host: Apple M5 Pro, Python 3.11.15, scipy 1.17.1) + standard prototype-vs-native reasoning
findings.scope: every wall-clock number produced by the sbsh_scene physics modules
findings.limitations: n/a — this IS the limitation record.
findings.framework_consequence: Any future experiment that cites sbsh physics timings must state 'Python-prototype constants' and re-measure against a Rust/C core before a real-time claim. Registered in both physics solver components' known_limitations.
findings.open_questions: A Rust-core graduation (SpatialRegime + Yannakakis + the solvers behind hymeko_pgraph) would fix the constants — may touch CORE.YAML, escalate.

findings.claim: HTL existed as THREE non-interoperating evaluators: Rust hymeko_monitor (STL+Until, combinator-only, no text parser), Python hymeko_neuro/eval/htl (G/F only, scalar-smuggled structure, has a parser), and per-scenario `condition "..."` strings in .hymeko parsed by ad-hoc policy evaluators. They are unifiable because the coupling to RL is at the edges (signal sources + reward consumer), not the core.
findings.confidence: measured (code map + one-engine parity)
findings.scope: the HTL/temporal-monitoring subsystem
findings.limitations: unification delivered on the Rust engine; Python consumers reconciled opt-in in v2, not retired.
findings.framework_consequence: One engine (htl.engine): a single parser + robustness algebra. New consumers import it; do not add a 4th evaluator.
code_changes: hymeko_monitor: formula/parse.rs, signal.rs, builders.rs; hymeko_monitor_ir crate; data/meta/meta_monitor.hymeko

findings.claim: The Rust engine reproduces the incumbent Python evaluator's robustness to 1e-9 on the real galambos spec (single-event robustness_at) AND on streaming HtlMonitor traces. This parity gate is the REQUIRED evidence before backing/retiring the Python RL path.
findings.confidence: measured (1e-9 across corpus + galambos + streaming)
findings.scope: scalar-signal HTL (the whole production consumer surface)
findings.limitations: parity proven on the tested corpus, not every possible formula/signal; custom Python registry predicates are not backed.
findings.framework_consequence: Any move to make Rust the Python HTL backend (or retire pure-Python) is GATED on this parity staying green. Default backend stays 'python'.
findings.open_questions: retire pure-Python / flip HtlRewardSpec default — deferred until RL runs finish + explicit user OK.

findings.claim: Python's anytime/PAST-window `robustness` and the Rust forward settled-edge `StlMonitor` are DIFFERENT monitoring semantics (backward window vs bounded-future settling); they do NOT agree for streaming. Matching Python's streaming monitor requires a faithful port of the past-window semantics (eval_at::robustness_history), not the forward monitor.
findings.confidence: measured (streaming parity to 1e-9 after the port)
findings.scope: streaming HTL monitors (episode verdicts, training-metric monitors)
findings.limitations: the two modes coexist deliberately; a formula picks the mode by which monitor/evaluator it uses.
findings.framework_consequence: The Python-facing PyHtlMonitor uses robustness_history (past-window). The forward StlMonitor is for bounded-future framework-side monitoring. Do not swap one for the other expecting equal streaming numbers.

findings.claim: Past-time operators (Historically/Once/Since) belong to the ANYTIME evaluator; the forward bounded-future StlMonitor cannot settle them and MUST reject them at construction rather than mis-evaluate.
findings.confidence: measured (rejection test + anytime goldens)
findings.scope: any StlMonitor construction
findings.limitations: past-time IS supported by robustness_history / PyHtlMonitor; the guard only blocks the forward monitor.
findings.framework_consequence: GUARD: StlMonitor::new returns MonitorError::PastTimeUnsupported on H/O/S; flatten arms are unreachable!() guarded by that check. Future forward-monitor callers get a loud error, not a wrong verdict.
findings.open_questions: past-time in the forward monitor (backward window sizing) — deferred v-next.

findings.claim: Multi-file .hymeko contexts (with @"..." imports + `using`) FAIL the naive single-file pipeline with UnresolvedRef; they require the canonical ModuleStore::compile (recursive import load into a shared interner + namespaced index + apply_usings + lower_program_to_ir). Import paths are relative to the importing file.
findings.confidence: measured (real triad_hri.hymeko now loads; was UnresolvedRef)
findings.scope: loading any imported .hymeko context
findings.limitations: a bare string has no base dir -> load_ir(str) stays single-file/import-free by design.
findings.framework_consequence: load_ir_file now routes through ModuleStore::compile; missing/broken imports surface as LoadError::Module (loud). Reuse this loader, do not re-run the single-file pipeline on imported files.
code_changes: hymeko_monitor_ir/src/lib.rs (load_ir_file via ModuleStore; LoadedIr enum; LoadError::Module)

findings.claim: HTL structural atoms can delegate to hymeko_query's pattern engine, gaining transitive-isa and signed-incidence pattern matching the trait builders cannot express. BUT the engine's compile/resolve require H:'static, so a borrowing Signal<IrState> cannot feed compile: dynamic-structure per-observe monitoring is precluded. For static contexts the structural facts are constant and computed once.
findings.confidence: measured (quadruped: 9 links via isa, monitored)
findings.scope: structural properties of a loaded (static) .hymeko context
findings.limitations: static-structure only (the 'static bound); node queries must filter Kind(Node); arity is post-filtered.
findings.framework_consequence: htl.query_atoms registered as the canonical structural-quantification path (reuse hymeko_query; builders.rs kept for cheap attrs). Dynamic-structure monitoring is an open lever (relax the monitor's 'static bound to a lifetime-parameterised trait object).
regression_tests: query_signal.rs tests (isa count, signed-ref pattern, arity, margin)
findings.open_questions: relax StlMonitor/resolve H:'static for Signal<IrState> (dynamic structure).

findings.claim: hymeko_query does NOT build with default-features=false: its always-compiled `transforms` module references the `interpret`-feature-gated `rewrite` module (an internal feature-coupling bug in that CORE crate). Consumers must keep default features.
raw_evidence: hymeko_query/src/transforms/mod.rs:233 (use crate::rewrite::...); hymeko_query/src/lib.rs:35-36 (#[cfg(feature=interpret)] pub mod rewrite)
findings.confidence: measured (E0433 on default-features=false)
findings.scope: any crate depending on hymeko_query
findings.limitations: hymeko_query is CORE lockdown:implementation; the fix (feature-gate transforms too, or move rewrite) is a core edit, NOT done here.
findings.framework_consequence: GUARD (recorded): depend on hymeko_query with DEFAULT features. hymeko_monitor_ir/Cargo.toml carries the note. parser is already a transitive dep so the footprint is unchanged. A future core fix should gate transforms behind interpret or move the rewrite ref.
regression_tests: the crate building at all (default features)
findings.open_questions: core fix in hymeko_query to allow a lean default-features=false consume (needs a CORE approval).

findings.claim: [SUPERSEDED 2026-07-15 by F-PP-009 — the rollout-anchor did NOT close the gap (x1=0.458); true cause is off-policy critic value-overestimation, abstraction is sound] The pick-place residual-SAC collapse (0.875 base → 0.458) is ISOLATED to F-SAC-5 (rollout-state covariate shift), NOT the critic/entropy confound. Applying the F-SAC-1/3/4 fix alone (--sac-rehab: init_alpha 0.1, lr 3e-4, ANNEAL entropy) left the critic BOUNDED (0.427 vs the AUTO run's 11-21) and α annealing, yet it STILL collapsed to 0.458 (identical Δ -0.417). So critic/entropy stabilization is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT; with a stable critic + no entropy pressure the off-policy SAC still drifts on its own rollout states. This is exactly why on-policy PPO held (trains on its own states) and off-policy SAC does not.
findings.source_experiment: 2026-07-15 pick-place RL pitfall audit (sac-rehab decisive test)
findings.confidence: measured (1 seed, 40k; identical final to the AUTO baseline with a bounded critic)
findings.scope: off-policy SAC over the residual pick-place env; confirms the coin-toss F-SAC-5 generalizes to pick-place
findings.limitations: 1 seed; the rollout-anchor fix (F-SAC-5) is being tested now to confirm it closes the gap. REFUTED by F-PP-009: rollout-anchor x1/x5/x20 and DAgger all failed; the collapse is critic overestimation, not covariate shift.
findings.framework_consequence: The rollout-state DAgger anchor (F-SAC-5) is the evidence-backed lever for pick-place off-policy RL, not just a hypothesis. Added PickResidualExpertTeacher + --sac-rehab/--rollout-anchor to pick_place_residual_rl. The kato15 vetted spec is the rollout-anchor config, not vanilla SAC.
findings.superseded_findings: corrects the flat 'pick-place RL is a negative' reading (F-PP-002/003) — the collapse was under-diagnosed confounds, not fundamental
findings.open_questions: Does the rollout-anchor (running) stop the 0.458 collapse / beat 0.875? Verdict pending; then the kato15 multi-seed run.

findings.claim: SUPERSEDES F-PP-008. The pick-place residual-SAC collapse (0.875 base -> 0.458) is OFF-POLICY CRITIC VALUE-OVERESTIMATION, NOT an abstraction/interface bug and NOT F-SAC-5 covariate shift. A 7-check abstraction audit PASSES: executed = clip(base + delta*tanh(mu), lo, hi); zero-residual reproduces base exactly (0.875, HARD GATE); teacher/base/actor read identical raw obs; the teacher residual is a FUNCTION of obs (near-obs residual gap 0.001 vs norm 0.197); the anchor lives in the same [-1,1] residual space the env receives; the target is excellent (reactive-teacher-residual closed-loop = 1.000, v3 expert = 0.958, both > base); residuals are well-calibrated. A high-capacity FEEDFORWARD BC of the reactive teacher reaches 0.792. SAC still collapses to 0.458 because the learned critic ranks the actor's own OOD near-saturated residual (|r|=0.707) at Q=-0.687 ABOVE the teacher/base/random residuals (all Q ~ -1.16..-1.22); the -Q actor loss then drives the policy off the imitation basin. Anchor-strength x5/x20 and 7-round DAgger (-> 0.58) do NOT rehabilitate it.
raw_evidence: check5 zero-residual=base 0.875; C reactive-teacher closed-loop 1.000; part4 FF-BC 0.792; check8 Q(actor)=-0.687 > Q(teacher)=-1.164
findings.confidence: measured (deterministic probes; SAC single-seed but reproduces the archived 0.458 across AUTO/rehab/anchor x1/x5-not-run/DAgger)
findings.scope: off-policy SAC over the residual pick-place env; the mechanism (critic overestimation of OOD residuals) is general to actor-critic-over-a-frozen-base
findings.limitations: SAC runs are single-seed (RL carve-out: rest ranking claims on multi-seed); the FF-BC 0.792 uses the reactive-teacher distribution; the 0.79->1.0 clone gap (recurrence?) is an open question, not resolved here.
findings.framework_consequence: Before attributing an RL collapse over a frozen base to 'RL fails' / the scenario, run the ABSTRACTION AUDIT GATE: (1) zero-residual reproduces base; (2) reactive-oracle closed-loop ceiling; (3) FF-BC of the oracle; (4) critic Q-ranking teacher vs actor vs random. Only a critic that ranks the teacher >= the actor's own action clears the RL implementation. The vetted pick-place path is IMITATION (reactive-teacher BC = 0.792, -> recurrent) + a BC-dominant/conservative-critic refiner (TD3+BC via bc_coef, or CQL/IQL/AWAC), NOT vanilla SAC + rollout anchor. kato15 is justified only once a local config beats 0.875.
code_changes: hymeko_rl/experiments/pick_place_residual_rl.py: --anchor-coef knob (proved anchor-strength inert; kept for the record)
superseded_findings: F-PP-008 (attributed the collapse to F-SAC-5 covariate shift; refuted: rollout-anchor x1 = 0.458, DAgger = 0.58, cause is critic overestimation)

Does TD3+BC (bc_coef high) warm-started from the 0.792 BC clone hold >= 0.875 and refine past it?

findings.claim: The 0.792 feedforward residual-clone gap (vs reactive-teacher oracle 1.000) is EXECUTION-HARD at the contact discontinuity, NOT a temporal/history-information deficit. Multi-seed (3 seeds x 24 eval) over FF, history-stack K in {2,4,8}, and LSTM residual clones: ALL cluster at 0.75-0.83 median with overlapping ranges, NONE reaches base 0.875 (best Hist4 median 0.833), none reaches 0.95. More memory is not monotonically better; MSE is decoupled from closed-loop score. Mechanism (failure-mode inspection): the teacher residual is small on average (|r|~0.06-0.09) but has near-full-range discontinuities at contact-mode switches (grasp step-jump max 0.733); a smooth NN clone cannot reproduce the spike, so its executed-action error is largest at grasp (0.060 rad) and the dominant failure is grasp-then-DROP (irreversible). Side signal (weak, single-seed): LSTM reached 2.39cm precision (base 4.69, expert 2.16) -> recurrence may recover the expert's precision integral even where it does not lift the success rate.
findings.source_experiment: 2026-07-15 recurrent/history residual-clone gap test (Step 1 after F-PP-009)
raw_evidence: multi-seed medians FF .750 Hist2 .792 Hist4 .833 Hist8 .792 LSTM .792 (all < base .875); grasp max-jump 0.733
findings.confidence: measured (3 seeds x 24 eval, fixed eval tasks; ranges overlap -> architectures indistinguishable)
findings.scope: residual imitation clone of a contact-rich (grasp) task; the contact-discontinuity execution-hardness is general to residual clones over frozen bases on hypersensitive contact tasks
findings.limitations: 3 seeds; GRU dropped from multi-seed after worst single-seed; the precision (2.39cm) signal is single-seed and not confirmed
findings.framework_consequence: GATE for warm-starting RL from an imitation clone on a contact task: the clone must reach base BEFORE adding a critic. Here no history/recurrent clone reaches base -> TD3+BC is NOT justified (would warm-start below base, hit the same contact-spike wall, and F-PP-009 critic over-estimation would drag it off). Recurrence helps PRECISION (place-err) not SUCCESS RATE on contact tasks -> pick the metric with headroom. Candidate levers not yet run: mode-gated residual (zero residual during grasp/lift via active_modes), or a precision track. Do NOT close the residual line; do change the target.

open_questions: Does a mode-gated residual (RL only in smooth approach/place-align phases) preserve base while removing the grasp-spike failure?
Does the LSTM 2.39cm precision replicate across seeds (precision track vs success track)?

findings.claim: Mode-gating the pick-place residual is separable at GRASP but not at LIFT. Gated-oracle sweep (reactive teacher): ALL=1.000; all_but(grasp)=0.875 (=base, residual separable at grasp -> base handles grasp); all_but(grasp,lift)=0.708 (<base -> the lift residual, |r|~0.095 + discontinuous, is LOAD-BEARING and un-gate-able). A grasp-gated FF clone (3 seeds) rises to median 0.792 [0.75,0.833] from non-gated 0.708 (gating removes the grasp-then-drop failure) but STILL < base 0.875 (the now-active lift discontinuity becomes the bottleneck). Lever-1 ceiling = base; it can preserve/protect but NOT beat base.
raw_evidence: scratchpad/mode_gated_sweep.py (oracle by mode-set) + scratchpad/mode_gated_clone.py (3-seed grasp-gated clone)
all_but(grasp)=0.875, all_but(grasp,lift)=0.708; grasp-gated clone median 0.792 vs non-gated 0.708
findings.confidence: measured (oracle sweep deterministic-ish n=24; clone 3 seeds)
findings.scope: residual over the frozen pick-place base; the grasp-separable/lift-load-bearing split is task-structural (contact coupling)
findings.limitations: grasp-gated SAC (RL, not clone) not run -- its ceiling is already base, so it cannot beat base regardless; single mode-set family tested
findings.framework_consequence: Improving stable-place RATE via a residual over this frozen base is EXHAUSTED -- three independent angles converge: off-policy critic over-estimation (F-PP-009), execution-hard clone gap at contact discontinuities (F-PP-010), and the un-gate-able load-bearing lift residual (this finding). Mode-gating (the coin-toss 'structured residual' regime) preserves/protects base but CANNOT beat it here because pick-place phases are contact-coupled (unlike coin-toss). Do NOT close the residual line; CHANGE THE TARGET to precision (place-error), the only metric with headroom (LSTM 2.39cm vs base 4.69, expert 2.16) -- lever 2.

open_questions: Does grasp-gated SAC HOLD base (neutralize the F-PP-009 collapse) even though it cannot beat base? (structural, not improvement)
Precision track (lever 2): does the LSTM 2.39cm precision replicate multi-seed?

findings.claim: From-scratch (non-residual) RL on 7-DOF pick-place hits an OPTIMIZER-AGNOSTIC exploration wall. Cached from-scratch PPO (2026-07-09/10) never grasps ('reward can't bootstrap pre-grasp'). New: from-scratch SAC (off-policy replay + AUTO-entropy exploration + dense pick_place_aligned reward, symmetric critic, 80k steps) ALSO never grasps AND never even reaches (reach=grasp=lift=0.00 from untrained through 80k). The place=0.375 is a metric-inflation artifact (boxes spawn near target; idle arm trips placed_stable; grasp=0 disproves real placing). An asymmetric critic cannot fix this -- exploration, not value-learning, is the blocker (symmetric SAC never reached). Random exploration cannot discover a grasp on 7-DOF contact; replay cannot learn a grasp never in the buffer.
findings.source_experiment: 2026-07-15 from-scratch SAC exploration-wall test (capstone of the pick-place RL arc)
raw_evidence: scratchpad/from_scratch_sac.py (NormActionEnv, build_sac symmetric AUTO-alpha, pick_place_aligned reward)
findings.confidence: measured (single 80k SAC run, converges with cached multi-run PPO failure + theory)
findings.scope: from-scratch RL on 7-DOF contact manipulation; the exploration wall is general to sparse-discovery contact tasks
findings.limitations: single SAC run at 80k (smoke budget); a vastly larger budget is not justified given cached PPO failure + dominating scripted expert
findings.framework_consequence: The pick-place RL space is FULLY MAPPED and bounded by two structural walls: (1) SETPOINT wall -- residual RL holds base 0.875 but cannot beat it (F-PP-009/010/011); (2) EXPLORATION wall -- from-scratch RL never discovers a grasp, optimizer-agnostic (PPO+SAC). Imitation->RL (BC warm-start) is the ONLY viable learned path and IS the deployed base. No RL lever with real headroom remains. Deploy the scripted v3 expert (0.958/2.16cm, dominates) for best performance, or the FF-DAgger base / LSTM-BC clone for a learned policy; residual RL only to HOLD base safely (structured+mode-gated+conservative critic), never to beat it. GUARD: do not re-propose from-scratch RL for this task class without a demonstration/curriculum that seeds the grasp.

regression_tests: (none -- negative result; the guard is this finding)
open_questions: Would a curriculum / demonstration-seeded exploration (e.g. RRT-seeded replay, grasp-primitive bootstrap) break the exploration wall? (out of scope; the scripted expert already dominates)

findings.claim: The pick-place stable-place success metric (placed_stable/reached, used arc-wide via LiftPlaceMetric) has a ~0.458 IDLE-inflation floor: a zero-action policy scores reached=0.458 while ever-grasped=0.000 (verified 2026-07-16). Cause: placed_stable requires only the box within place_radius (6cm) at rest for settle_dwell -- NOT grasping or lifting -- and the object spawns within place_radius of the target ~46% of episodes. The FF-DAgger base scores reached=0.875 but the clean lift-requiring 'delivered' (legacy, held-above-target) =0.000 and its ever-grasped=0.50. A SKILL-ISOLATING metric = placed_stable AND ever-grasped zeroes the floor (idle -> 0).
findings.source_experiment: 2026-07-16 SignedHypergraphLiNGAM role-1 diagnostic (surfaced the confound) + idle/base verification
raw_evidence: verified: FF base reached=0.875/grasp=0.50/delivered=0.00; IDLE reached=0.458/grasp=0.00 (N=24, seed0=20000)
env pick_place_env.py:716-727 (placed_stable = box in place_radius at rest, no lift/grasp required)
findings.confidence: measured (idle + base, N=24; converges with from-scratch untrained place=0.375)
findings.scope: the FANUC pick-place stable-place metric; object spawn sector overlaps the target
findings.limitations: a single benchmark's spawn geometry; the floor value (~0.4-0.46) varies with seed set
findings.framework_consequence: GUIDELINE, NOT A HARD GATE (user directive 2026-07-16). When interpreting pick-place stable-place numbers, be AWARE of the ~0.458 idle floor and PREFER reporting a skill-isolating metric (placed_stable AND ever-grasped) or the idle floor alongside the absolute number. Do NOT hard-fail evals on it. The arc's QUALITATIVE findings HOLD (walls, SAC destructive, clones cap, expert dominates -- relative comparisons on the same metric); the absolute numbers overstate skill by ~the floor. This SHARPENS F-PP-009: 'SAC collapse to 0.458' = collapse to the do-nothing floor = TOTAL skill destruction (grasp->0), not 'holds half'. Future benchmark revisions could widen the spawn-target separation to remove the floor at source.
regression_tests: (advisory guideline; no hard gate per user)
open_questions: Re-express the arc's key numbers (base/clones/oracle) on the skill-isolating metric for a clean ladder?

findings.claim: SignedHypergraphLiNGAM role-1 diagnosis: on the skill-isolating metric (placed_stable AND ever-grasped), ONLY the DAgger'd base has real skill (0.42, grasp 0.56). The LSTM BC-only clone = 0.00 (NEVER grasps -- BC covariate shift; its cached 'reliability 0.917' was pure metric inflation) and the collapsed residual SAC = 0.00 (grasps 0.12, never completes; its '0.458' ~ the idle floor). The per-policy signed causal hypergraph (DirectLiNGAM -> A+/A-) formally confirms ONLY the base has a real grasp->success chain (grasp->target +1.49); the LSTM and SAC have DEGENERATE DAGs (grasp/success constant-0 -> dropped). The pooled deviation->grasp F-PP-009 probe is CONFOUNDED by policy heterogeneity (edge +0.000; reverse grasp->deviation -0.59) -- a clean causal test needs within-policy deviation variation, not cross-policy aggregates.
raw_evidence: FF skill 0.42 grasp 0.56; LSTM/SAC skill 0.00; per-policy DAGs; pooled deviation->grasp +0.000
findings.confidence: measured (N=48/policy, single seed set; DAG edges are PROPOSALS per CIP doctrine)
findings.scope: pick-place FF-DAgger/LSTM/SAC; the causal machinery over rollout aggregates
findings.limitations: single seed set; DirectLiNGAM proposes (ablations decide); the F-PP-009 probe is confounded (unanswered here)
findings.framework_consequence: (1) The framework's signed causal hypergraph WORKS as a control diagnostic -- it surfaced the metric confound (F-PP-013) and formally shows only the DAgger'd base has a real skill chain. (2) A causal GATE/ENSEMBLE over {FF,LSTM,SAC} (the user's roles 2/3) is UNDERCUT: only FF has real skill (0.42), LSTM/SAC ~0, so a gate would just pick FF -- mixing buys nothing until a SECOND policy has real complementary skill. (3) BC clones roll out to ~0 real grasp (covariate shift, the known BC failure) and the inflated metric MASKED this (re-examine clone claims on the skill metric). (4) To causally test F-PP-009, use within-policy deviation variation; the direct Q-ranking evidence for F-PP-009 stands independently.

findings.claim: Rollout-state DAgger (query the reactive teacher on the policy's OWN visited states, aggregate, re-clone) CLOSES the flat-action covariate collapse: BC 0.417 -> DAgger 0.75 median (0.625-0.792), 3 seeds, zero harmful, on the floorless PlanarGrasp coin-delivery (Gate 0 teacher-recovery 0.917).
findings.confidence: measured, 3 seeds, all positive
findings.scope: flat-action reactive-teacher coin-delivery; the covariate mechanism (F-SAC-5) is general
findings.limitations: imitation recovers the teacher ceiling (~0.75 at beta=0), does not surpass it; the general loop is train.dagger.Dagger, not the experiment's private copy
findings.framework_consequence: On-policy imitation on visited states is the flat-action rescue. Canonical component = hymeko_rl/train/dagger.py::Dagger (imitation.rollout_state_dagger).
findings.open_questions: Does beta-mixing / more iters reach the ~0.9 demonstrator ceiling?

findings.claim: DAgger-anchored SAC does NOT refine past the DAgger flat policy: 0/3 seeds' online actor beats DAgger (online 0.17-0.46 vs DAgger 0.625-0.792); rollback always recovers the DAgger checkpoint. The rollout-anchor gradient is live and DOMINANT (norm 3.9-7.3 vs Q 1.7-2.6), yet the SAC objective still pulls the online policy off the greedy DAgger optimum.
findings.confidence: measured, 3 seeds, 0/3 positive
findings.scope: SAC refinement on top of a DAgger-recovered flat policy
findings.limitations: AWAC/IQL and stronger refiners were de-authorized (out of scope by the hard stop)
findings.framework_consequence: Closes 'RL refinement of a DAgger flat policy expands the frontier'. The rollout anchor STABILIZES (prevents the ~0 collapse) but does not expand -> sac.rollout_state_dagger_anchor = RESEARCH_ONLY. Guard: no RL frontier-expansion claim on the flat coin-toss abstraction.

findings.claim: Dwelling into F-SAC-8: the DAgger-anchored-SAC failure is a WITHIN-SAC covariate shift, not mistuning. action_mean stays == teacher on DEMO states (demo_bc_loss 0.004) but DRIFTS 25x on the policy's own ROLLOUT states (rollout_teacher_bc_loss 0.10); the rollout anchor DOMINATES the update direction (cos_vs_full 0.965) yet LOSES, and val decays from the DAgger start (0.5-0.75) to ~0.375. Mechanism: SAC's exploration (sigma>0) breaks the self-consistency that makes DAgger work (label on GREEDY-visited states == eval states) — the anchor is computed on STOCHASTIC-rollout states while delivery is graded on the GREEDY trajectory. Exploration re-opens the covariate gap imitation removed.
findings.source_experiment: dwelling into F-SAC-8 (analysis of rollout_dagger_results.json, NO new run)
findings.confidence: MEASURED discriminants (demo 0.004 vs rollout 0.10 bc-loss, cos 0.965, val decay, 3 seeds); INFERRED exploration-covariate mechanism (not directly isolated) — EXPLORATION HYPOTHESIS REFUTED by Arm C (F-SAC-10).
findings.scope: RL refinement of an imitation-optimal policy on a floorless task
findings.limitations: REFUTED by the Arm C greedy-rollout discriminator (F-SAC-10): greedy rollouts do NOT rescue the policy (median 0.21 vs DAgger 0.75), so exploration/self-consistency was NOT the cause. The exploration hypothesis here is retained as the motivated-but-wrong inference; the confirmed mechanism is F-SAC-10.
findings.framework_consequence: Generalizes: exploration-based RL is self-defeating on an imitation-optimal floorless policy — exploration re-introduces the covariate shift imitation removed, and an anchor on the stochastic-rollout distribution cannot close a gap defined on the greedy-eval distribution. Guard: do not expect on-policy RL to refine a DAgger-optimal flat policy; the self-consistent greedy-DAgger loop (imitation.rollout_state_dagger) is the lever. Deepens/subsumes F-SAC-8's 'anchor dominant yet loses' into a covariate explanation.
findings.open_questions: Answered by F-SAC-10 (the -Q/critic term, not exploration).

findings.claim: The mechanical constraint schema is DERIVABLE per-step from the MuJoCo contact solver (not hand labels): active contacts -> constraint Jacobian J_m via mj_jac -> SVD rank/nullspace -> motion projector P_m=V0 V0^T, stick/slip, pivot axis, guards. On a passive tip the admissible-motion dimension walks d_perp = 6 -> 3 -> 1 -> 0 (FREE -> sticking-vertex -> EDGE_PIVOT 1-DOF hinge -> FACE_REST 0-DOF); projector idempotency ||P-P^2|| <= 3.3e-16 every frame (3 seeds); derived guard-crossings agree with the simulator's own contact events within debounce; labels bit-reproducible.
findings.confidence: measured (3 seeds, deterministic; 23 tests)
findings.scope: single rigid freejoint body on a plane in MuJoCo
findings.limitations: AMBIGUOUS rank-transition path unit-tested only (0/200 on the fast drop); TWO_SUPPORT/JAMMED reserved not emitted on a single surface.
findings.framework_consequence: schema.constraint_extractor registered CANONICAL; the benchmark's ground truth is physics-derived, not annotated. Future C-gates import extract_schema for the privileged schema/projector.
findings.open_questions: AMBIGUOUS in situ needs a slow controlled pivot (a later gate).

findings.claim: Counterfactual identifiability of a hidden physical schema is achievable on the cuboid substrate: the sliding friction mu is invisible in BOTH the raw kinematics AND the instantaneous derived mode (a resting box is FACE_REST for any mu; mu is latent below the mode). Measured (N=24 matched pairs): R0 flat AUC 0.500 CI(0.5,0.5) with obs-match 0.0 (matched pairs byte-identical), privileged AUC 1.0; R1 a bounded reversible probe recovers it (mu_lo slides ~8.7mm vs mu_hi ~0.30mm, ~29x, probe AUC perfect, 100% reversible/no tip); R2 passive-wait |d|max 6.84e-9mm below sensing resolution -> the probe is NECESSARY. The anti-'flat-reveals-everything' guard for the benchmark.
findings.confidence: measured (N=24 matched pairs, bootstrap CIs; 10 tests)
findings.scope: hidden sliding-friction schema on a cuboid on a plane; the matched-counterfactual+probe pattern generalizes to other hidden physical parameters
findings.limitations: identifiability only; recognition from PARTIAL/NOISY observation (a learned estimator) is C2, not shown here.
findings.framework_consequence: probe.constraint_counterfactual registered CANONICAL; C2 (schema recognition from partial obs) is authorized and constrained by this finding (a flat instantaneous observer is at chance -> a learned recogniser must beat it).
findings.open_questions: Is mu recognisable from ProbeResponse.com_traj under partial+noisy sensing (C2)?

findings.claim: A tip must be measured as an ORIENTATION change (up-axis tilt > threshold), NOT a schema-mode transition. A sliding flat box transiently shows FREE/EDGE derived modes from contact-point sampling flicker WITHOUT rotating; a mode-based tip detector would falsely flag it tipped and mis-score reversibility.
findings.confidence: measured (independently rediscovered by a de-risk pass in a second session)
findings.scope: any tip/topple detection over a contact-mode signal
findings.limitations: orientation threshold (15 deg) is a calibrated cutoff.
findings.framework_consequence: GUARD: tip detection uses _uptilt_deg / ProbeResponse.tipped (orientation), never a mode-label transition. Regression pins that the sliding low-mu box is NOT tipped.

findings.claim: A 'signal below the noise floor' claim must be a MAGNITUDE test, not a scale-blind rank statistic. Rank-AUC (Mann-Whitney) is scale-invariant, so on the numerically-zero passive-wait displacement (~1e-9 of the probe signal) it reports a spurious ~0.30 separation; the physically meaningful statement is that a passive observer sees nothing resolvable (passive |d|max < sensing resolution AND << probe median).
findings.confidence: measured
findings.scope: any 'necessity / signal-vs-noise-floor' evaluation; general to scale-invariant rank metrics on near-zero signals
findings.limitations: resolution threshold (0.1mm) is a stated sensing bound.
findings.framework_consequence: GUARD: the R2 'probe necessary' verdict gates on magnitude (passive_max < resolution_m AND < 0.05*probe_median); passive AUC is reported but explicitly NOT gated on. Reusable rule: do not use rank-AUC to argue a signal is absent.

findings.claim: MuJoCo combines contact friction as the MAX of the two geoms' friction, so setting a hidden mu on the object alone is overridden by the floor's friction (the effective friction stays pinned by the load-path contact). The variable hidden-friction schema must be set on the LOAD-PATH contact (floor + object).
raw_evidence: de-risk: object-only mu -> no slide separation; floor+object mu -> Coulomb separation
findings.confidence: measured (de-risk sweep: effective friction pinned at 1.0 until floor mu lowered)
findings.scope: any MuJoCo env with a hidden per-body friction schema
findings.limitations: MuJoCo-specific (friction-combination = elementwise max unless geom priority is set).
findings.framework_consequence: GUARD: set_sliding_mu is applied to contact_geoms = object + floor; a friction-schema env must vary the load-path contact, not one geom. Reusable MuJoCo gotcha.

findings.claim: Tip-vs-slide under a SUSTAINED push is NOT cleanly friction-separable in MuJoCo: dynamics/momentum dominate and the box tips across a wide mu range (measured: identical tip outcome for mu 0.12-0.9 at F=2.5N). The friction-separable constraint-schema transition is SLIDE-vs-STAY (FACE_REST d_perp=0 <-> FACE_SLIDE d_perp=3) under a bounded sub-tipping COM push, matching Coulomb theory (boundary mu~0.46 at F=0.9N, predicted 0.459).
raw_evidence: de-risk sweep (scratchpad): sustained top-push tips for all mu; bounded COM push separates slide/stay at mu~0.46
findings.confidence: measured (de-risk sweep over mu x force)
findings.scope: friction counterfactual design for the constraint-schema benchmark; general to sustained-push vs quasi-static contact
findings.limitations: scoped to the sustained-wrench probe; a quasi-static controller could make tip-vs-slide separable.
findings.framework_consequence: DESIGN CONSTRAINT: a friction counterfactual must use slide-vs-stay, not tip-vs-slide; tip/pivot-feasibility counterfactuals require a quasi-static controller (a later gate). Constrains future C-gate probe design.
code_changes: informs constraint_probe design (safe_probe_force sub-tipping window); no separate code artifact
findings.open_questions: Is tip/pivot feasibility separable under a quasi-static controller (a later gate)?

findings.claim: A learned estimator recovers the constraint schema (stick/slip verdict under a standard probe, boundary mu*=F/N=0.70) from a PARTIAL, NOISY observation of the probe response (COM trajectory + Gaussian position noise), beating the flat baseline and approaching the privileged ceiling. First benchmark gate closed by a FITTED model. Measured (N=60, mu~U(0.20,1.20) continuous, 5-fold held-out): probe 0.906 balanced-acc at sigma->0 vs flat 0.500 (chance), approaching privileged ceiling 0.891 (R1); probe-flat CI(0.182,0.517) excludes 0 at 2mm noise (R0); graceful degradation 0.906->0.888(2mm)->0.808(5)->0.688(10)->0.647(20), above flat throughout (R2). The 5-trajectory-feature learned estimator slightly EXCEEDS the 1-feature (exact-disp) privileged at low noise (shape carries boundary info); the sub-1.0 ceiling is boundary-blending near mu*, the honest signature of a non-trivial task.
findings.confidence: measured (N=60, 5-fold held-out, 7-sigma sweep; 9 tests)
findings.scope: binary stick/slip schema recognition on the cuboid substrate; the partial-observation recognition pattern generalizes
findings.limitations: recovers a BINARY verdict, not the continuous projector P_m (that is C3); one probe direction, one fixed force; featurization+classifier experiment-resident (extraction flagged for C3).
findings.framework_consequence: probe.constraint_counterfactual bumped to 1.1 (com_traj/tangential_traj = the partial-observation signal). C3 (projector estimation) authorized; C3 lands the probe_features extraction so C2/C3 share one observation model.
findings.open_questions: Can the continuous projector P_m / d_perp / pivot axis be recovered from partial state (C3)?

findings.claim: A linear classifier on physical-unit (metre-scale, ~1e-3) features MUST be standardized (StandardScaler in the pipeline); an unscaled LogisticRegression under default L2 underfits to the majority class and returns EXACTLY 0.500 even on cleanly-separable privileged input. The bug was caught because the PRIVILEGED CEILING (which must be near-perfect) was implausibly at chance: the privileged/oracle observer is a sanity tripwire -- if it is at chance, the harness is broken, not the task.
findings.confidence: measured (privileged 0.500 -> 0.891 after adding the scaler)
findings.scope: any linear classifier on physical-unit features; general to scale-sensitive estimators + oracle-ceiling sanity checks
findings.limitations: specific to scale-sensitive linear models (tree/standardized models unaffected).
findings.framework_consequence: GUARD: schema recognizers use make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression()); the privileged/oracle ceiling is a required sanity tripwire (measure it first; at-chance oracle => harness bug). Generalizes the eval-integrity 'measure the ceiling first' rule with a concrete scaling catch.

findings.claim: The greedy-rollout ablation (Arm C, single-variable vs Arm B: env stepped with action_mean, no exploration) REFUTES the exploration hypothesis (F-SAC-9): greedy-online median 0.208 vs DAgger 0.75, 0/3 hold, no better than stochastic Arm B (0.25). Restoring rollout self-consistency does NOT rescue the policy. The culprit is the -Q / off-policy CRITIC, not exploration: the DAgger policy is an IMITATION optimum, not the critic's Q-optimum, and the -Q gradient (a critic that extrapolates badly off the narrow DAgger manifold, still probed by the sampled-action actor loss even under greedy rollouts) pulls the actor off the DAgger optimum faster than the demo+rollout anchors (coef 2.5) hold it. RL refinement of an imitation-optimal flat policy fails at VALUE ESTIMATION, not exploration.
findings.confidence: MEASURED single-variable 3-seed ablation (0/3 greedy hold; median 0.21 vs 0.75). The precise -Q-sampling-vs-critic split not fully isolated (a deterministic -Q ablation would pin it further).
findings.scope: off-policy actor-critic refinement of an imitation-optimal flat policy
findings.limitations: greedy_rollout changed only the ENV STEP; the actor loss still samples actions for -Q, so 'exploration' at the actor-loss level is not fully removed. But the ROLLOUT-covariate hypothesis is cleanly refuted.
findings.framework_consequence: Corrects F-SAC-9. Same failure class as F-PP-002 (offline actor-critic collapses the pick-place clone) -> a general guard: do NOT refine an imitation-optimal policy with off-policy actor-critic on a floorless task; the value drift degrades it regardless of exploration. Lever = the self-consistent DAgger loop (imitation.rollout_state_dagger). greedy_rollout added to SACConfig as a reusable diagnostic.
findings.open_questions: Would a deterministic -Q (DDPG-style, no actor-loss sampling) or a constrained/pessimistic critic (CQL/IQL) hold DAgger? (out of scope by the hard stop)

findings.claim: The mechanical-schema motion projector P_m (d_perp, nullspace V0) is a DISCONTINUOUS function of pose at contact boundaries (adding/removing a contact changes d_perp discontinuously), so pose-only projector estimation is FRAGILE to sensor noise at the contact-detection scale. Measured (N=40 passive drops, sigma-sweep 0-20mm): naive geometric d_perp balanced accuracy 1.000 at sigma=0 (projector Frobenius error 0.000); the projector error JUMPS 0.000->0.933 at just 1mm (contact eps=2mm) -> 0.986 at 2mm; principal angle -> 37deg at 2mm; naive d_perp acc collapses to 0.498 at 20mm. A learned standardized-logistic classifier is noise-FLAT (~0.73): it robustifies above ~2-5mm but caps below the clean geometric extractor (1.00) and the privileged ceiling, worst on the rare transient (edge/vertex) modes.
findings.confidence: measured (N=40 drops, 6-sigma sweep; 9 tests)
findings.scope: pose-only projector/d_perp estimation on the passive cuboid substrate; the discontinuity is general to contact-mode schemas
findings.limitations: pose-only (Option A); a probe-informed estimator is untested; the loaded/slip projector is flicker-noisy (de-risk).
findings.framework_consequence: schema.constraint_extractor bumped to 1.1 (projector_frobenius_error + principal_angles_deg metrics). Motivates a probe-informed projector estimator (force/contact sensing) rather than pose-only for the loaded projector. Does NOT refute the probe -- the fragile regime is exactly the contact transitions where the C1/C2 probe is the natural signal.
findings.open_questions: Does a probe-informed projector estimator (com_traj + probe_features) beat the pose-only fragility?

findings.claim: Pose-only projector / admissible-subspace estimation must NOT be trusted near contact transitions: the projector is discontinuous there (F-CSB-9), so any pose-sensor noise at the contact scale jerks the projector error to ~1 and flips d_perp. Robust recovery of the loaded projector needs force/contact sensing (the C1/C2 probe), not pose alone.
findings.confidence: measured (proj err 0.93 at 1mm across 40 drops)
findings.scope: pose-only projector estimation on the passive substrate; scoped closure -- NOT a universal impossibility (probe-informed Option B untested)
findings.limitations: the loaded/slip projector is flicker-noisy (de-risk); a quasi-static controller could clean it.
findings.framework_consequence: GUARD: a future projector estimator should use force/contact sensing near contact transitions, not pose alone. The probe-informed estimator (reuse com_traj + land probe_features) is the recorded open lever (C4/C5).
findings.open_questions: probe-informed projector estimation (the direct next lever).

findings.claim: The recognised mechanical schema is CAUSALLY LOAD-BEARING for control. A supervised schema-conditioned controller (probe -> fitted belief -> calibrated push force) on a push-to-target-band task (net COM disp in [30,45]mm, no tip; the correct force depends on hidden mu) matches the oracle and dominates every schema-blind / belief-ablated arm. Measured (N=40 held-out): oracle 0.925 = schema 0.925 (recognition 0.99) >> flat 0.500 > frozen 0.425 >> swapped 0.000; placement error schema 4.0mm vs swapped 36.7mm; F_A=0.90N F_B=1.40N. The swapped-belief collapse to 0 (worse than schema-blind flat 0.50) is the decisive signature: success is a FUNCTION of the belief (a wrong belief is worse than no belief). First positive CONTROL gate; supervised (no RL).
findings.confidence: measured (N=40 held-out seeds, calibration held out; 8 tests)
findings.scope: schema application on the robust 1-D slide-vs-stay mechanism (F-CSB-6) with a calibrated force-per-class controller; the causal method generalizes
findings.limitations: 1-D lookup controller (not MPC); supervised calibration; schema application, not continuous multi-phase execution (C5).
findings.framework_consequence: C1->C2->C4 closes the recognition->application loop for the friction schema. The schema-conditioned controller pattern (probe->belief->calibrated force + freeze/swap ablations) is demonstrated; the controller is experiment-resident (extract when C5 reuses it). RL (C6) must beat this supervised ceiling to be authorised.
findings.open_questions: Continuous multi-phase execution (C5); a projector-informed controller where C3 pose is fragile.

findings.claim: A schema-application / control gate must include belief FREEZE + counterfactual-SWAP ablations to prove the schema is causally LOAD-BEARING (not merely correlated/present). A schema that is present but not load-bearing would still let a flat/frozen controller succeed; the decisive signature is SWAPPED-WORSE-THAN-FLAT (inverting the belief inverts the action -> worse than no belief, C4: swapped 0.00 < flat 0.50).
findings.confidence: measured (the verdict's two honest-negative branches are regression-locked)
findings.scope: any schema-application/control gate in the benchmark (and generally, causal attribution of a belief/representation to a control decision)
findings.limitations: the ablation proves causal dependence, not optimality; the belief must be manipulable (freeze/swap).
findings.framework_consequence: GUARD/METHOD: schema-controllers must be evaluated with freeze + counterfactual-swap belief ablations; report swapped vs flat. Registered as the causal-attribution method for the constraint-schema control gates.

findings.claim: The hidden mechanical schema (box mass) is NOT load-bearing for the continuous pivot-to-a-target-face. The pivot EXECUTES (passes through EDGE_PIVOT 100%, tips one face 0.99) but an adequate FIXED force + the OBSERVABLE balance-point release tips one face for ANY mass: N=40 oracle 0.99 = schema 0.99 = flat 0.99 >> open_loop 0.84 (no feedback); frozen=swapped 0.50 (a WRONG force fails, so force magnitude matters at the extremes, but a single max-adequate force (2.2N) covers both classes). So the pivot is controllable from observable geometry + an adequate action; hidden-parameter (mass) recognition earns no control credit. Echoes C3 (pose-determined projector); contrasts C4 (hidden friction WAS load-bearing for the single-step slide, swapped->0).
findings.confidence: measured (N=40 held-out seeds; 9 tests; deterministic pivot verified run1=run2)
findings.scope: the minimal external-wrench one-face-pivot task; closure scoped -- a harder pivot regime (narrow corridor / slip-during-pivot / obstacle) is untested (C5-prime)
findings.limitations: 1-face pivot with a calibrated lookup controller; not MPC; not a universal impossibility.
findings.framework_consequence: Closes hidden-schema-conditioned pivot control for this task. GUARD: a schema-CONTROL claim must include an OPEN-LOOP (no-feedback) arm + an observability check -- if a fixed adequate action + observable feedback suffices, the hidden schema is not load-bearing. The balance-release pivot controller (realises the Galambos mode transition) is experiment-resident; extract if a C5-prime reuses it.
findings.open_questions: A harder pivot regime where observable feedback fails and the hidden schema could earn control credit (C5-prime).

findings.claim: The hidden schema's CONTROL value is TASK-SPECIFIC across the C0-C5 arc: it is load-bearing for RECOGNITION (C1 identifiable / C2 recogniser) and for SLIDE control under genuine ambiguity (C4, swapped-belief->0.00), but NOT for the POSE-DETERMINED projector (C3) or the OBSERVABLE-FEEDBACK pivot (C5, schema=flat=oracle). The hidden schema earns CONTROL credit only where the action is a fine parameter choice under ambiguity the observation cannot resolve; where observable feedback + an adequate action suffice, it does not.
findings.confidence: measured across five gates (C1-C5)
findings.scope: the constraint-schema benchmark; the principle (hidden-schema control value = ambiguity the observation cannot resolve) generalizes to schema/belief-conditioned control
findings.limitations: synthesized from this benchmark's tasks; the boundary (when is the control-relevant quantity observable) is task-dependent.
findings.framework_consequence: DESIGN PRINCIPLE + METHOD for schema-control gates: (1) include an open-loop / observable-only baseline; (2) claim schema-control value only when the control-relevant quantity is NOT observable and freeze/swap degrades. Directs future gates toward regimes with genuine observation-unresolvable ambiguity.
